title: U.S. customary units: how many in one?
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Recipes, road signs, lumber and gas pumps in the United States all use these units. Knowing how they nest inside each other lets you double a recipe, measure a room or read a map without reaching for a calculator.

How to hold it: Learn each family as one chain, since the units nest: teaspoon, tablespoon, fluid ounce, cup, pint, quart, gallon (3, 2, 8, 2, 2, 4). Draw it once as nesting boxes, a big G with four Qs inside, two Ps in each Q and two Cs in each P: picture plus words. Then length (12, 3, 5,280), weight (16, 2,000) and area (43,560, 640). Say each fact as a sentence, "one gallon is four quarts," and quiz yourself both ways.
